key_expressions: Do you have a moment for a consultation?,
I have a question about the assignment.,
The explanation was a bit confusing.,
Could I get some career advice too?,
Is this a good time for you?,

A: Professor, do you have a moment for a quick consultation?
There was a part of today’s assignment explanation I didn’t quite understand.
Could you go over it briefly one more time?
B: Of course! Which part was confusing for you?
A lot of students ask about that section.
Let me walk you through it slowly.

A: I still find the report structure a bit difficult.
I’m not sure what order I should write it in.
I think an example would help me understand better.
B: That’s totally normal. It can be confusing at first.
Just follow a simple introduction–body–conclusion format.
I’ll upload a sample document on the course page.

A: I wanted to check if my presentation topic is going in the right direction.
I’m worried the scope might be too wide.
If I need to revise it, I can adjust it right away.
B: Your topic looks good! Not too broad and not too narrow.
If you narrow the examples to two or three, it’ll be clearer.
With that small adjustment, your presentation will be strong.

A: Would it be possible to review the questions I got wrong on the last exam?
I want to understand exactly where I made mistakes.
If you give me some feedback, I think I can improve next time.
B: Sure, reviewing incorrect answers is really helpful.
Most of your mistakes just need a bit of concept reinforcement.
Hold on, I’ll bring your exam sheet.

A: Could we schedule a separate consultation sometime this week?
I also have questions about my major, not just the assignment.
I can adjust to whatever time works best for you.
B: Wednesday afternoon works for me.
For major-related counseling, preparing some notes beforehand helps.
But feel free to choose a time that suits your schedule.

A: Your feedback on my presentation was really helpful.
After making the changes you mentioned, it sounds much smoother.
Could you check it one last time if possible?
B: I’m glad to hear that! Great job applying the feedback.
It’s almost complete in its current form.
We can do a final check right after class.

A: I read the paper you recommended last time.
It was more interesting and helpful than I expected.
I think I’d like to look for some similar materials.
B: Oh, you already read it? Impressive!
If you understood that paper, the next ones won’t be difficult.
I can recommend a few more if you’d like.

A: Could I get some information about the project schedule later this semester?
I want to know how much preparation time I’ll need.
Planning ahead will help me avoid rushing.
B: Good idea! Planning early makes things easier.
The project will start after the midterm exam.
I’ll announce the detailed schedule next week.

A: Professor, would career counseling also be possible?
I’m not sure which direction I should prepare for.
I want to build a solid foundation step by step.
B: Of course! I’m always happy to help with career guidance.
The most important thing is finding a field you’re genuinely interested in.
If you want, I can help you create a personalized curriculum.

A: Thank you so much for today’s consultation.
I feel much more at ease after hearing your advice.
I’ll follow the direction you suggested and prepare gradually.
B: I’m really glad to hear that!
Take your time, there’s no need to pressure yourself.
And feel free to come back anytime you need help.
